description: Iran is not a party to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961. Legalisation for use in or from Iran must go through consular legalisation.
notes: Check whether Iran has acceded since this was written - accession would materially change this row.

description: Sworn translation, then Iranian Ministry of Justice, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then the destination country's embassy. Typically 10-20 working days per document type.

aspect: The Farsi original must stay attached
description: The translation must be certified and legalised together with the original, and the Farsi original must remain physically attached at every step. Separating them invalidates the chain.
energy_note: One clerical slip restarts the whole sequence.

description: A man who cannot return to Iran - conscription, political risk - cannot walk the chain himself. It must be done by a relative with power of attorney, which itself must be legalised through the same chain.
money_note: Agent or relative costs, courier, repeat fees.
energy_note: A recursive dependency on the country you left.

description: Incomplete files are placed on hold and kept open until the missing document arrives. A missing stamp produces indefinite limbo rather than a clean refusal that could be appealed.
energy_note: No decision to push back against.

description: Iranian export rules cap hand-woven carpet at 24 square metres per traveller, caviar at 125g and saffron at 150g - a reminder that what a family can carry out is itemised by the state down to the gram.

aspect: SCENARIO - the power of attorney loop
description: Omid needs his birth certificate legalised. He cannot enter Iran. He must send his uncle a power of attorney - which must itself be notarised in Toronto, legalised by Global Affairs, then by the Iranian consulate, then couriered. Elapsed time before the actual task can begin: eleven weeks.
energy_note: Eleven weeks of queueing for permission to join a queue.
